subject: Tiered trial loop detected — Sylvanaitech
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Suspicious sequence: Sylvanaitech tiered trial requests

Markus,

Monitoring flagged an unusual sequence of trial/grant activity tied to Sylvanaitech over the past 48 hours. Three separate email identities (elena.martinez@, sam.cho@, and a third account) received overlapping 30-day promo credits; they were created from the same device fingerprint and two IPs within the same /24. Allocation timestamps are within minutes of each other.

I pulled a condensed events export and attached the CSV for review. Suspect this is a coordinated tiered trial pattern to extend evaluation credits across product groups.

[Attachment: events-sybil-log.csv (CSV, 120KB)]

Can we gate further automatic promo grants to that account until we confirm? Recommend pausing any additional self-serve credits for Sylvanaitech.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-20T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Suspicious sequence: Sylvanaitech tiered trial requests

Thanks Ben — good catch.

Please hold on any further automated promo grants to Sylvanaitech immediately. Ben, can you apply a temporary block in the promo engine for the account and mark the HubSpot company record with a fraud flag? Link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/78910

Karthik / Monica — can you triage the attached events and surface the top three indicators (IP overlap, device fingerprint, email similarity) and confirm whether this meets our fraud threshold for coordinated trials? If yes, recommend suspension of any pending credits and escalation to Legal for contract enforcement.

Cc'ing Monica to loop in Customer Success if we need to pause access. Keep the thread tight — I'll author the escalation note if needed.

-Markus
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-03-21T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Suspicious sequence: Sylvanaitech tiered trial requests

Hi Markus / Ben,

Appreciate the heads up — and sorry for the confusion. Sylvanaitech recently spun up three product teams (Search, Summarization, and Rerank) on separate evaluation tracks. Each team requested a short trial independently because they were working against different product deadlines and billing contacts. That explains the close timestamps.

We did not intend to abuse promo credits. Happy to provide our business registration, tax ID, and a single procurement contact to consolidate future grants: procurement@slvanaitech.com (TBD: procurement contact name is Elena Martinez).

If you need anything else to validate that this is one company with distinct internal teams, let me know — we can share additional account-level info or a signed MSA to get the proper entitlements.

Thanks,
Sam Cho
Engineering Manager, Search
Sylvanaitech

Date: 2028-03-22T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Suspicious sequence: Sylvanaitech tiered trial requests

Markus / team,

I dug into the event traces and here's the summary (top indicators):
- IP overlap: three account creations came from 18.204.23.0/24 within a 36-minute window.
- Device fingerprint: identical browser UA + canvas fingerprint for two of the identities.
- Email patterns: two addresses use different subdomains but tie to the same corporate MX.
- Token usage: rapid token consumption on composite evals, then new trial requests within 24–48 hours.

Attached is a sanitized export of grant activity with timestamps and hashed device fingerprints.

Recommendation: treat as coordinated tiered-eval behavior. Pause auto-grants, require single procurement contact and signed TOS/MSA for any additional credits. If they provide a valid procurement contact + business registration we can consider a manual one-time consolidation. Otherwise, escalate for enforcement.

[Attachment: trial-grant-activity.json (JSON, 54KB)]

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Cho <sam.cho@sylvanaitech.com>, Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@sylvanaitech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-28T16:44:00-07:00
Subject: Decision: Temporary promo freeze + verification request — Sylvanaitech

Sam / Elena,

Thanks for the prompt reply and for offering procurement details. After internal review we are applying a temporary freeze on further automated promo grants to Sylvanaitech while we complete a short verification. This is a standard step when device/IP signals indicate potential coordinated trial extension.

What we need from you to lift the freeze ASAP:
1) Procurement contact name and email (please confirm Elena Martinez / procurement@sylvanaitech.com).
2) Business registration / tax ID (PDF).
3) If available, a signed MSA or PO that covers consolidated trial entitlements — we can provision a short-term manual credit while legal reviews.

If you can provide the above within 5 business days we will perform a manual consolidation and issue a one-time limited promo grant to cover the active evaluations. Without that, promo grants will remain suspended until verification completes (estimated up to 10 business days).

Ben/Finance (Priyom) — please hold billing actions but prepare a manual credit path if they submit the MSA.

Sam — appreciate the transparency here. We want to keep you running, but we have to protect the promo program from coordinated extension. If you want to accelerate, send procurement docs to: compliance+trial@redwood.ai and cc me.

Best,
Markus Klein
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
